From c0e310188299358279fc27c88512f94db78991a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 08:57:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
index 0b12d5023800..7b3d6c12ad61 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
@@ -453,6 +453,9 @@ static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c`**
   - A new check was added at the beginning of the `enable_signaling` function to determine if the `active` fence is a barrier. If it is a barrier, the function returns early without proceeding further. This prevents unnecessary operations on barriers that do not require signaling.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a specific issue related to the handling of barriers in the i915 driver. By adding the check for barriers, the patch ensures that the flush operation is only attempted on valid fences, thus preventing potential inefficiencies or errors when dealing with barriers. This change is a direct response to the bug identified in the previous commit (`d13a31770077`) and is intended to improve the robustness of the signaling mechanism within the driver.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect handling of barriers in the i915 driver, where an attempt to flush a barrier could occur even when it is not appropriate to do so. This can lead to ineffective flush operations, as barriers do not require signaling like regular fences do. The lack of a check to differentiate between barriers and valid fences resulted in potential inefficiencies and errors during the signaling process.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
 
 	dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
 	dma_fence_put(fence);
 }

The bug occurs because the code attempts to enable signaling on a barrier without checking if the active fence is indeed a valid fence. This can lead to ineffective flush operations since barriers do not require signaling like regular fences do, resulting in potential inefficiencies and errors.

Reason:
The fix introduces a check to determine if the active fence is a barrier before attempting to enable signaling. If it is a barrier, the function returns early, preventing any unnecessary and ineffective flush operations, thus ensuring that signaling is only attempted on valid fences.
